How to recognise it: The visible opening tapers toward both corners and reads longer than tall.
What to observe: Look at the overall outline with eyes relaxed and facing forward.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike a round-looking opening, the visible height does not dominate the outline.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, check the open eye in a mirror and keep any placement aligned with the tapered outline. This is a general option, not a requirement.

How to recognise it: The visible opening reads more open and circular, with height standing out as much as the horizontal span.
What to observe: Look at the amount of visible opening above and below the iris when your face is relaxed.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike prominent-looking eyes, this label describes the opening’s outline rather than how forward the eye area appears.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, assess the result while looking straight ahead so the visible opening remains the thing you are evaluating. This is a general option, not a rule.

How to recognise it: With the eye relaxed, upper-lid skin partly covers or reduces the visible crease area.
What to observe: Look at the crease with eyes open normally, not only when the brow is lifted.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike a monolid, a crease may exist but be partly hidden when the eye rests.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, test it with the eye open and relaxed so you can see what remains visible. This is a general option, not a product instruction.

How to recognise it: No distinct upper-lid crease is visibly separated from the lid when the eye is at rest.
What to observe: Look for a continuous lid surface rather than trying to locate a hidden fold.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike hooded eyes, the distinction is the lack of a separate visible crease rather than a crease being covered.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, place and review it with the eye open as well as closed. This is a general option, not a requirement.

How to recognise it: The outer corner reads higher than the inner corner when you look straight ahead.
What to observe: Compare the inner and outer corners on the same eye; do not use a tilted selfie.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike almond, this describes corner direction; an eye can be both almond-looking and upturned.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, use the corner direction as the reference point rather than assuming every eye needs the same line. This is a general option.

How to recognise it: The outer corner reads lower than the inner corner when you look straight ahead.
What to observe: Compare corner position on a level, front-facing view.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike hooded, this describes the corner direction, not the amount of visible lid crease.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, review the result with the face level and eyes open. This is a general option, not a correction rule.

How to recognise it: The eye area reads visually farther back under the brow area.
What to observe: Look at the relationship between brow area, upper lid, and the apparent depth around the eye.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike hooded, this is about perceived depth rather than whether a crease is covered.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, test visibility in ordinary light rather than judging only a close-up mirror view. This is a general option.

How to recognise it: The eye area reads visually more forward from the surrounding socket area.
What to observe: Observe the apparent projection in a level, relaxed view rather than a close, wide-angle photo.
How it differs from a nearby label: Unlike round, this is about perceived forwardness rather than the shape of the visible opening.
Common appearance-focused direction: If you use makeup, make small changes and check the open eye from normal viewing distance. This is a general option, not a product rule.

How to recognise it: One eye or one feature can fit a different label from the other, or several labels can apply at once.
What to observe: Record each eye separately: opening outline, crease visibility, corner direction, and perceived depth.
How it differs from a nearby label: This is not a failed classification. The labels describe separate features that can overlap.
Common appearance-focused direction: When using any appearance-focused technique, check each eye separately and keep only changes you prefer. This is a general option.
